solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boast about compound somewhere in the Midlands

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to crow is to boast
an ester is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: Someone brags about a walled compound they own in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' reads as an enclosure but is the chemistry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is a cathedral city in the West Midlands region of England, so it is one example of a place there.

clue.text: Put on clothing that’s ultimately inferior

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is wanted
clothing wraps around a body, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: put on clothes, in the past tense
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone dons clothing that turns out to be poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The S is the last letter of "that's", so the same word both supplies a letter and links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, meaning lower in quality, which matches inferior as an adjective.

clue.text: Correspondence Italians swapped regarding business streamlining

indicators.note: things swapped have changed places, so these letters trade positions

blocks.note: a ratio expresses a correspondence between quantities
taken as written
on, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Letters exchanged by Italian executives discuss slimming down a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' suggests letters, but it is the mathematical sense of a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Rationalisation is the reorganising of a company to cut waste and cost, making its operations leaner and more efficient.

clue.text: Testimony from key study probing immorality

indicators.note: a probe pokes inside something, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: E is a musical key
vice is wickedness
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Evidence given in court comes from an important investigation into wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key study' reads as a crucial piece of research, but the words split into a musical key and a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given by a witness is a form of proof presented in court, the ordinary sense of evidence.

clue.text: Attempt to acquire a sleeveless garment for burlesque

indicators.note: whatever acquires something takes it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
taken as written
a vest is a sleeveless undergarment or top

explanation.surface: A performer tries to get hold of a vest for a comic stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burlesque' sits at the end looking like the reason for the vest, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation or parody, which is what a burlesque does to its serious subject.

clue.text: Go on, take it … no pressure!

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: to presume is to take something as given
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes a friend gently to accept an offer, promising there is no obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is spoken encouragement; 'take it' is really 'suppose', PRESUME, which loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to continue after a pause, which is exactly what it means to resume an activity.

clue.text: Succeeded after initially disregarding rotten tips

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only a first letter is kept
coming after means placed later in the line, so this piece follows the others

blocks.note: first letter of the word
food that is off has gone rotten
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded by ignoring bad advice from tipsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten tips' looks like bad advice; 'tips' is really the verb for raising your hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip your hat is to lift it in greeting, and to doff a hat is the same courteous gesture.

clue.text: Excellent result for champion

blocks.note: def is slang for excellent, from definitive
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A title-holder gets a great outcome in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' reads as a noun, the winner, but is the verb meaning to stand up for.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support and speak up for it, which is to defend it against attack.

clue.text: Energy in fire might not be dispersed temporarily

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it, so one letter joins the rest
things dispersed are scattered about, so the letters end up in a new order

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Energy trapped in a fire may stay contained, for now at least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might not be' reads as grammar but is simply part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: For the time being means for now but not permanently, an idiomatic phrase equivalent to the adverb temporarily.

clue.text: Just one snitch spilled the beans

blocks.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
let on means revealed a secret

explanation.surface: Only one informer ever revealed the secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just one' looks like it describes the snitch; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single item on its own, such as one card of a suit in a bridge hand.

clue.text: Wine from lidless container knocked back

indicators.note: without a lid means the top is missing, so the first letter goes
knocked back means sent backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a canister without its first letter

explanation.surface: A drinker gulps wine straight from an open container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking quickly, which fits the surface, but it signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, so it is one kind of wine.

clue.text: Stigmas at heart causing indignity, mostly

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so the middle letter is taken
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: the middle letter of the seven
an affront is an insult or indignity, less its last letter

explanation.surface: Social stigmas lie at the core of what makes people feel humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stigmas' reads as marks of disgrace; it is the botanical sense, the parts of a flower that catch pollen.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice is made from the dried stigmas of the crocus flower, so the stigmas themselves are what you buy.

clue.text: Ham in the end became speck

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a mote is a speck of dust

explanation.surface: A piece of ham eventually shrank to a mere speck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like meat, and speck is also a German cured ham, but here it is the verb for overacting.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to overact theatrically, and to emote is to show emotion in an exaggerated, showy way.

clue.text: Guys in hamlet manufactured cheese

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it, so one piece sits within another
something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so these letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: guys are men
taken as written

explanation.surface: Village men produce cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' tempts as the Shakespeare play; it is the small village, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese with large holes, so it is one example of a cheese.

clue.text: Lack of transport in southern metropolitan area

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a car is a form of transport
a city is a metropolitan area

explanation.surface: A southern city suffers from poor public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lack of' tempts as the whole definition, but 'of' is a link and the definition is just 'Lack'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarcity is a shortage, the state of there not being enough of something, which is a lack.

clue.text: Disorganised mafiosi centrally involved in violent mob clash

indicators.note: centrally means at the middle, so the central letter is chosen
to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it
violence throws things around, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the middle letter of seven
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gangsters caught up in a brutal street fight are hopelessly disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter from the middle of 'mafiosi' joins the eight letters of 'mob clash' before they are rearranged. Shambolic is informal British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic means chaotic and badly run, like a shambles, which is to say thoroughly disorganised.

clue.text: Immediately provides some info

blocks.note: first meaning: at once, the medical instruction from Latin statim
second meaning: a statistic, a single piece of data

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sentence about someone giving information quickly; the two ends are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors say it for urgent action at once, and it is also informal shorthand for a statistic or figure.

clue.text: Husband had trouble accepting the first of many nasty messages

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
had a meal, that is ate
to ail is to trouble or afflict
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A husband struggled to cope with receiving a lot of abusive letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had trouble' reads as one phrase meaning struggled, but it splits in two: had as in ate a meal, trouble as in afflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive or threatening letters or emails sent to someone, which are nasty messages.

clue.text: It’s shifted inside lorry with skill

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase standing for an adjective, fair because both describe work done skilfully

indicators.note: shifted means moved around, so the letters change places
inside means placed within, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
an artic is an articulated lorry, the British name for a large truck

explanation.surface: A load is being moved skilfully into a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is a truck in British English, and an artic is an articulated one.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistic describes work made with creative skill, so the phrase acts as a loose adjectival equivalent.

clue.text: A short film showing great passion

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its ending

blocks.note: taken as written
a video, cut to its first three letters

explanation.surface: A brief movie depicts intense romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A short film' looks like a unit, but 'short' only trims the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager and enthusiastic, so someone avid is keen with great passion for something.

clue.text: Farm workers finally produce sweetcorn after flood retreats

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so last letters are taken
to retreat is to go backwards, so the letters run the other way
coming after means placed later in the line

blocks.note: a flood of things is a myriad, a huge number
the last letters of both words

explanation.surface: Farmhands manage to grow corn once the floodwater recedes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flood' suggests water, but it is the sense of a great many, as in a flood of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairymen work on dairy farms milking cows and handling milk, so they are one type of farm worker.

clue.text: Grant is like Leo?

blocks.note: as means like, in the manner of
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Is someone called Grant similar to someone called Leo?
explanation.walkthrough: Grant and Leo pose as men's names; the question mark flags that Leo is an example of a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign something is to allot or give it formally, as when you grant property or rights to someone.

clue.text: Shows distress about small emergencies

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: someone distressed cries
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone gets upset over minor emergencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small emergencies' reads as one phrase, but 'small' is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are times of acute danger or difficulty needing urgent action, the plural of crisis.

clue.text: Money that is covering either empty restaurant

indicators.note: something emptied keeps only its shell, so only the outer letters stay
to cover is to go over and around, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: brass is British slang for money
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Cash is found to be protecting one or other deserted eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money that is' is read as two pieces run together, and that pair then wraps round the emptied word; brass is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant, so it is a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Plant overturned military intelligence plot

indicators.note: to overturn is to flip over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: MI abbreviates Military Intelligence, as in MI5
a plot of garden ground is a bed

explanation.surface: A mole overturns a spy agency's scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'plot' both suggest espionage, but plot is a garden bed and plant is to set firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to fix it firmly in a surrounding mass, which is to embed or imbed it.

clue.text: Live and be successful, but with an absence of love

indicators.note: an absence of something means it is missing, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: to do well is to succeed
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Life advice: thrive, even if you go without romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' reads as romance but is the tennis score, zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or make your home there, which is to live there.

clue.text: Groups of ordinary people put down endless connections

indicators.note: endless means with no end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: laid, meaning put down, without its final letter
ties are connections or bonds

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk are dismissing their endless networking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests belittling; it is simply placing, so laid.
explanation.definitionFit: A laity is the body of ordinary people as opposed to clergy or professionals; laities are several such bodies.

clue.text: Scandinavian girl beginning to enjoy riding a bike so?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: Astrid is a common Scandinavian girl's name
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian girl is starting to enjoy cycling, perhaps sitting like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the girl on the bike; the question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with one leg on each side, which is how a cyclist sits on the saddle of a bike.

clue.text: Standard chapter, unattributed

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter
anon, short for anonymous, marks an unattributed work

explanation.surface: A normal chapter carries no author's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard chapter' reads as a routine section of a book; the definition is only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a general rule or principle by which something is judged, a benchmark or standard.

clue.text: Small and badly fitted with one metal frame for drying material

indicators.note: to be fitted with something is to have it installed inside

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
the Roman numeral for one
a cage is a framework of metal bars

explanation.surface: A small, poorly installed metal rack is used for drying fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests cloth, but here it means substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica gel is a porous form of silica that absorbs moisture, so it is used as a desiccant in packaging.
